judgments.reasoning_cat1: Notices 'may' be given by listed means 'or otherwise', and 'All notices, demands and requests hereunder may be made orally, to be confirmed promptly in writing' leaves both the permissiveness and the effect of a missing written confirmation open. 'Promptly' and 'or otherwise' are nameable soft terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs margin calls under Paragraph 4 (c025, c027), where timing and form of notice are critical, and Paragraph 17 (c056) demands writing for waivers and modifications; the interplay is workable but leaves oral margin calls contestable. No flat contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any existing agreements between the parties containing general terms and conditions for repurchase transactions' is a limited supersession whose scope is arguable, and the severability sentence is boilerplate. Moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits awkwardly with the replacement Paragraph 12 (c085), which expressly ties this Agreement to 'all other agreements or transactions' between the parties, and with Annex I ¶15 (c094) covering pre-existing Transactions. Those need reconciling.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Assignment prohibition and the termination-with-survival carve-out are stated plainly. Nothing ambiguous to name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 15(b) (c054) carves out assignment of Paragraph 11 sums and Annex I ¶15 (c094) extends the Agreement to existing Transactions; both are compatible. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow, precisely targeted carve-out from the assignment ban. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly qualifies 15(a) (c053) and matches Paragraph 11's payment obligations. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard New York choice of law excluding renvoi. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex I ¶14 (c092) adds a consistent New York forum clause, though Annex I ¶5 and 5(e) contemplate Hong Kong and UK tax law questions; no operative conflict. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Anti-waiver and writing-for-modification language in conventional form, with a specific saving for delayed margin notices. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The writing requirement sits against oral Transaction formation in 3(a) (c022) and oral notices in Paragraph 13 (c051), but those concern formation and notice rather than modification. Modest tension only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An ERISA notice-and-representation mechanic, clearly expressed, ending with an express right not to proceed. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subparagraph (b) (c058) is expressly made subject to its last sentence, so the two mesh. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'most recent available audited statement' and 'most recent subsequent unaudited statement' are objectively ascertainable. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly subordinated to 18(a)'s last sentence and supported by 18(c)'s deemed representations. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'material adverse change in Seller's financial condition' is a classic elastic phrase, though here in a narrow ERISA context. Some intrinsic softness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits 18(a) and (b) and feeds Paragraph 11(vi)'s misrepresentation Event of Default without contradiction. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory characterisation with express carve-outs for inapplicable security types or terms; the carve-outs are self-limiting rather than ambiguous. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex I ¶10 (c087) adds a parallel FIRREA characterisation that is consistent, and Paragraph 6 (c032) already hedges the sale/loan question. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An acknowledgement that Paragraph 11 remedies are contractual liquidation rights under the Bankruptcy Code. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Paragraph 11 and Paragraph 19(a); nothing in Annex I cuts against it. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditional characterisation applying only if a party is an insured depository institution; plainly framed. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Annex I ¶9's FIRREA depository-institution provisions and ¶10. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: FDICIA netting characterisation with an express exception where a party is not a 'financial institution'. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the netting mechanics of Paragraph 12 as replaced (c085). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure disclosure of SIPC's position, imposing no obligation. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the other disclosures and with Annex I ¶6's broker-dealer agency arrangement. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat statement that SIPA gives no protection in the specified case. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits the surrounding disclosures; no operative provision contradicts it. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Disclosure that funds are not insured deposits; purely informational. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Paragraph 19(c) and Annex I ¶9. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble dates the Master Repurchase Agreement 'as of September 20, 1997' although the Agreement itself is dated September 20, 1998 — a mechanical error going to which instrument the Annex supplements. It also cites 'Paragraph |' rather than Paragraph 1.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its priority rule ('Supplemental Terms and Conditions shall prevail') drives the conflicts elsewhere — notably the reversal of 3(b) by ¶3 (c070), the deletion of Paragraph 12 by ¶8 (c085) and the pricing source in ¶7 (c084) against Market Value (c011). Whether the misdated reference undermines that priority is a live question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause says 'In addition to this Annex I and Annex II, the following Annexes ... shall form part of the Agreement' and then lists 'None', which is coherent if inelegant. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The body refers to 'any other annexes identified herein or therein' (c001) and Paragraph 10 to an agency annex; the blank fill here forecloses them consistently. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line restatement of intent that all Transactions are sales and purchases. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 6 (c032) contemplates the contrary characterisation as a fallback and grants a deemed security interest, so the two must be read together; that is a hedge rather than a contradiction. Modest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The amendment is a single sentence flipping the priority to the Confirmation; its own wording is unambiguous. Nothing to name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly reverses the last sentence of Paragraph 3(b) as printed (c023) while the body text remains in the instrument, and it also lets a Confirmation override the Agreement even though 3(b)(v) permits only terms 'not inconsistent with this Agreement'. That circularity is a genuine internal inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The renumbering instruction is garbled — adding subparagraph '(a)' 'before the word Seller' and referring to subparagraph 'S(ay' — so the amended text must be reconstructed. That is a mechanical defect on its face, albeit partly a scanning artifact.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restructures Paragraph 5 (c031), which is cross-referenced by the Purchase Price definition (c016) and Paragraph 8 by its old clause numbering ('clause (ii) of Paragraph 5'); after renumbering those references become uncertain. That is a real knock-on incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It uses capitalised terms that are never defined — 'LIBOR Rate' and 'Business Day' — and 'Taxes' where the definitions supply only 'Tax', and the gross-up proviso capping Seller's recovery cuts against the preceding gross-up obligation. Several nameable defects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its LIBOR-plus-1% interest for a Buyer's failure to remit overlaps the default-interest rule in Paragraph 11(h) (c048), and 'Income Payments' overlaps the Paragraph 2(f) definition of Income (c007). Reconciling the two interest and income regimes takes work.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'reasonably satisfactory', 'reasonably requested' and the forfeiture sentence ('Failure to comply with or perform any tax covenant ... will terminate payor's obligation') are broad but conventional. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the gross-up in 5(b) (c072) and coordinates with the Tax Event mechanism in 5(d) (c074) without contradiction. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'substantial likelihood' is inherently vague, and the enumeration is mislabelled — clauses appear as (i), (11) and (ii) — so the third limb's identity and its reference to 'such other party' are muddled. Nameable defects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It creates a deemed Repurchase Date not captured by the Repurchase Date definition (c018), which lists only Paragraph 3(c) and 11, and treats notice as a 3(c) demand (c024). Modest incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It uses 'Defaulting Party' as a capitalised defined term, but this Agreement defines only 'Event of Default' and speaks of the lower-case 'defaulting party' — an imported term that does not fit. The Stamp Tax Jurisdiction test is otherwise detailed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The undefined 'Defaulting Party' must be mapped onto Paragraph 11's defaulting party (c039, c043), and the indemnity for enforcement costs overlaps 11(h)(i) (c047). Reconcilable but not seamless.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mislabelled as '(i)' where the sequence calls for (f), but the definition itself — enactment or change in law or its official interpretation after trade date — is precise. Minor mechanical slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports the Tax Event definition in 5(d) (c074) accurately. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'includes any treaty, law, rule or regulation' is an inclusive rather than exhaustive definition, leaving edges open, but that is deliberate. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Change in Tax Law definition it serves. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any stamp, registration, documentation or similar tax' ends in a catch-all measured against three specifics — a small ejusdem generis point. Otherwise clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It serves only 5(e) (c075) and matches its usage. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any present or future tax, levy, impost, duty, charge, assessment or fee of any nature' is deliberately sweeping, and 'fee of any nature' could be argued to reach non-tax charges. A nameable breadth issue.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5(b) uses 'Taxes' rather than 'Tax', a small definitional mismatch, but the substance is consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The eligibility test is oddly framed: limbs (i) and (ii) are Hong Kong listing tests while (iii) applies only 'in the event that THORNBURG ... is a UK person or entity', a condition at odds with the named New Mexico corporation. The conditional structure is confusing but each limb is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex I ¶6 assumes Thornburg is a U.S. person while this clause contemplates it being a UK person, and the 'Notwithstanding any provision' opener overrides Confirmations that may describe other securities. That mismatch is a genuine, if peripheral, internal tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional obligation that CSFB Corporation confirm each Transaction on the Purchase Date; the condition and duty are stated plainly. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 3(b) (c023) requires Buyer or Seller (as agreed) to deliver the Confirmation, so who must confirm differs between the body and the Annex; the Annex prevails but the two must be read together. Modest conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It says the Agent will issue 'all required confirmations and statements ... in compliance with Rule 15c3-1', but Rule 15c3-1 is the net capital rule and has nothing to do with confirmations — a citation error that changes what the obligation means. That is a nameable mechanical defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expands on ¶6.a (c081) and is limited by ¶6.b(ii)'s liability disclaimer (c083); nothing in the body contradicts it beyond the confirmation-delivery point in 3(b). Modest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The disclaimer is broad but carves out gross negligence, wilful misconduct and securities-law non-compliance, and 'no responsibility or personal liability' is clear enough. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It confers rights and burdens on CSFB Corporation, a signatory only 'solely in its capacity as agent' and not a Buyer or Seller, which must be squared with the two-party structure and Paragraph 10's 'as principal' representation (c038). A real but secondary tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It names three screen sources and then, where no price is available, makes CSFB (Hong Kong) or 'one of its affiliates' the pricing source — a one-sided valuation power with no standard of reasonableness attached. 'If a price is not available' is itself an elastic trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts across the Market Value definition (c011), which requires a 'generally recognized source agreed to by the parties', and against Paragraph 11(e) (c044), which gives the nondefaulting party (which may be Seller) the sole discretion to establish the source. Those three cannot be harmonised without choosing a winner.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any other agreement or transaction whatsoever' and 'all transactions and agreements between them' are unbounded catch-alls that convert any outside default into an Event of Default, and the security interest reaches all property 'transferred ... pursuant to this Agreement or otherwise'. The breadth is nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces Paragraph 12 (c050), adds Events of Default beyond the closed list in Paragraph 11 (c039), and reaches outside agreements despite the supersession language in Paragraph 14 (c052). Several relationships require construction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional FIRREA record-keeping representation, with specific and verifiable content. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adds to the Paragraph 10 representations (c038) expressly and matches Paragraph 19(c) and Annex I ¶10. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Statutory characterisation language mirroring Paragraph 19(a), with the same self-limiting carve-out. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplements Paragraph 19 (c060) consistently rather than displacing it. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'substantially the same Securities' is undefined and elastic, and the notice timing ('at or prior to 10:00 am ... on such business day') has no clear antecedent for which business day is meant; the closing duty that Buyer 'shall offer Seller the right to terminate' is also unspecified as to terms. Several nameable soft points.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It layers a third substitution regime on Paragraph 9(a)'s consent requirement (c036) and 9(b)'s deemed consent (c037), and its opening condition ('does not have any existing right to substitute') may be defeated by 9(b) itself. That circularity is a genuine incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the loss incurred by Buyer directly arising or resulting from' a substitution, 'solely determined and calculated by Buyer in good faith', puts an open-ended measure in one party's hands. The good-faith qualifier is the only check.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It charges Seller with hedge and replacement-transaction costs on a substitution or termination, which sits against Annex I ¶13's bar on indirect and consequential loss (c091) and duplicates the Paragraph 11(h) damages measure (c047) outside default. Reconcilable only with effort.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short non-reliance representation with 'as it deems necessary' as the only soft phrase. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Paragraph 10's representations and the disclosures in Paragraph 20 without contradiction. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL LOSS OR DAMAGES' is the classic contested boundary, especially against hedge-unwind and replacement costs. The categories are named but their edges are notoriously disputed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 11(h)(ii)-(iii) (c047) expressly awards hedge-termination and replacement-transaction damages and 'any other loss ... directly arising', and Annex I ¶11(d) (c089) does the same on substitution, yet this clause says 'UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCES'. That is a direct clash a court would have to resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It submits to 'EXCLUSIVE JURISDICTION' but 'SOLELY FOR THE PURPOSE OF ANY SUIT ... BROUGHT TO ENFORCE ITS OBLIGATIONS HEREUNDER OR RELATING IN ANY WAY TO THIS AGREEMENT' — whether the exclusivity is a limit on the parties or only on the submission is arguable. That tension is nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the New York governing law clause (c055); Paragraph 11(i)'s preservation of other rights (c049) does not displace it. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard, unqualified jury waiver. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the forum clause immediately preceding it; nothing elsewhere contemplates jury trial. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence with no defined temporal or substantive limits: 'covers all Transactions in effect as of the date hereof' does not say on what terms pre-existing Transactions are converted. Its brevity leaves the retroactive effect open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Paragraph 14 (c052), which supersedes prior general terms and conditions, and with the misdated Annex preamble (c067) fixing 'the date hereof'; whether pre-existing Confirmations survive on their original terms is genuinely open. A real cross-provision question.
